claims.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys exhibit excellent mechanical properties at high temperatures.
Refractory high-entropy alloys commonly suffer from nonuniform or brittle native oxide scales that lead to rapid oxidation.
ALD can deposit an ultra-thin oxide such as Al2O3 or a doped variant on a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Applying an ALD oxide coating to refractory high-entropy alloys will enhance their high-temperature oxidation resistance.
A dense or continuous surface oxide film can improve the high-temperature oxidation resistance of refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed ALD oxide barrier will be self-healing.
The proposed ALD oxide barrier will limit oxygen ingress during high-temperature exposure.
Refractory high-entropy alloys are relevant to elevated-temperature aerospace and nuclear applications.
ALD will produce a uniformly deposited, defect-minimized, and highly adherent oxide film on the alloy.
ALD provides sub-nanometer control over the coating thickness.
ALD permits precise control of the oxide layer's composition and thickness.
Limiting oxygen diffusion through the coating will mitigate further oxidation.
The ALD coating will not adversely affect the alloy's underlying mechanical properties.
ALD-coated alloys will have a lower oxidation rate and slower oxide-scale growth than unmodified alloys.
ALD-coated alloys will retain their mechanical properties better than unmodified alloys under high-temperature conditions.
Unmodified refractory high-entropy alloys form nonuniform, poorly adherent oxide layers that cause rapid high-temperature degradation.
The coating's effectiveness depends on its remaining intact during thermal cycling.
Substrate chemistry or extreme operating conditions may cause the ALD layer to break down.
